problem:
Consider the quadratic form 
$Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}+6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}.$ 
Evaluate $Q(x)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

feedback.problem:
Consider the quadratic form 
$Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+2{x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{2}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3}^{2}.$ 
Evaluate $Q(x)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given that 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting this into the expression for $Q(x)$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+2{x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{2}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =(-1)^{2}+4\cdot (-1)\cdot 0+2\cdot (-1)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot {0}^{2}-2\cdot 0\cdot (-2)+(-2)^{2} \\  & =1+0+4+0-0+4 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
